text.p: These are the leading stories carried by Pakistani newspapers on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Wheat flour shortage has become acute in the southern port city of Karachi.
- An expert of Meteorological Department has forecast the pre-harvest loss of wheat crop on large scale due to prevailing country-wide torrential rains.
- Sixteen senior Customs officers have been suspended by the government from service for their alleged involvement in the palm oil import scandal.
- Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif expressed dissatisfaction over the construction quality on two sections of Lahore-Islamabad motorway and directed the Korean Daewoo Corporation to remove the fault.
- Pakistan anti-narcotics authorities are looking for a squadron leader of the Pakistan Air Force after one of his colleagues was arrested in New York for smuggling drugs, a police source said.
- The Pakistan People's Party has decided to launch an agitational movement against the government if the murder case registered against former prime minister Benazir Bhutto was not withdrawn.
- Benazir Bhutto has declined suggestions to seek bail before arrest in a murder case.

- The government borrowed 74.3 billion rupees from the banks to fill in budgetary gaps during the first nine months of fiscal 1996/97 (July-June) against the entire annual target of 44 billion rupees.

- The state-run Water and Power Development Authority (WAPDA) and Karachi Electric Supply Corporation are likely to increase their tariff rates by about 23 percent in one go before the next budgetary year starting July.
- The government has decided to start construction of several international airports on built, operate and transfer basis to attract foreign investors towards new industrial zones.
- A four-member delegation, headed by Finance Minister Sartaj Aziz will represent the country at the two-day Aid-to-Pakistan Consortium meeting beginning in Paris from April 22.
